title: Operator and base-change naturality of the formula
statement:
Use small ringed sites, unbounded derived categories of module sheaves, the canonical derived adjunctions, and ordinary uncompleted derived tensor. Let $R_X,R_Y$ be sheaves of commutative rings. For a morphism of ringed topoi $f:(\mathcal X,R_X)\to(\mathcal Y,R_Y)$ and $K\in D(R_X)$, $Q\in D(R_Y)$, write $\pi_{f,K,Q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] for the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes1)t_f$, with $t_f$ the canonical pullback-tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For bounded finite-projective coefficient complexes this is the arrow of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. In the reduction assertions, choose bounded finite-projective complexes $Q_n$ on $\mathcal Y$ with their strict-perfect packages, put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}Lf^*Q_n$, $\phi_n=\phi\otimes1$, $\pi_n=\pi_{f,K,Q_n}$, and let $\rho_n$ be the totalization arrow of that definition. If a reduction coefficient object $P_n$ is supplied with a strict-perfect representative $Q_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$, use that specified isomorphism and its derived pullback to identify these source and target objects with the reduction objects. All displayed reduction maps are in the ambient $R_Y$-module derived category, after restriction of scalars when necessary; no existence of a global strict-perfect representative for an arbitrary perfect sheaf complex is asserted.

For the base-change assertion, use a Cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] equipped with coefficient sheaves of commutative rings on its four small pro-etale sites and compatible inverse-image identifications, exactly as in [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Take $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R_X)$ and arbitrary $Q\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},R_Y)$. The exchange maps are the ambient ringed mates of that definition. In particular the square is commutative as a square of ringed topoi, not just on underlying schemes.

The projection-formula arrows are natural in $K$; hence for every
endomorphism $\phi:K\to K$ with reductions $\phi_n:K_n\to K_n$,

$$
Rf_*\phi_n\,\pi_n=\pi_n((Rf_*\phi)\otimes1),
\qquad
((Rf_*\phi)\otimes1)\rho_n=\rho_nRf_*\phi_n.
$$

For a Cartesian square, the following two routes are equal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
Lg^*((Rf_*K)\otimes^LQ)
&\xrightarrow{Lg^*\pi_f}Lg^*Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*Q)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_{K\otimes Lf^*Q}}
Rf'_*L(g')^*(K\otimes^LLf^*Q),\\
Lg^*((Rf_*K)\otimes^LQ)
&\xrightarrow{\sim}(Lg^*Rf_*K)\otimes^LLg^*Q
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_K\otimes1}
(Rf'_*L(g')^*K)\otimes^LLg^*Q\\
&\xrightarrow{\pi_{f'}}
Rf'_*(L(g')^*K\otimes^LL(f')^*Lg^*Q).
\end{aligned}
$$

The targets are identified by the chosen Cartesian isomorphism.

proof.text:
Fix $Q$ and $u:K\to L$. Write $F=Lf^*$, $R=Rf_*$, and $t=t_f$. The two morphisms $R K\otimes Q\to R(L\otimes FQ)$ in the naturality square have respective adjoints
$ (u\otimes1)(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)t_{RK,Q}$ and
$ (\varepsilon_L\otimes1)t_{RL,Q}F(Ru\otimes1)$.
The naturality of $t$ identifies the latter with $(\varepsilon_L F(Ru)\otimes1)t_{RK,Q}$. Counit naturality gives $\varepsilon_L F(Ru)=u\varepsilon_K$, so the adjoints agree. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves naturality of $\pi$ in $K$. Here the adjunction and its counit are those specifying the arrows, and the tensor comparison is the natural comparison in the cited tensor-pullback statement.

Apply step 1 with $u=\phi$ and $Q=Q_n$. By the definition $\phi_n=\phi\otimes1$ and the chosen reduction identifications, this gives $Rf_*\phi_n\,\pi_n=\pi_n(Rf_*\phi\otimes1)$. The totalization theorem applies because each chosen $Q_n$ is a bounded finite-projective complex with the package used to define its two arrows. It gives $\rho_n\pi_n=1$ and $\pi_n\rho_n=1$. Multiply the forward equality on the left and right by $\rho_n$ to obtain $\rho_nRf_*\phi_n=(Rf_*\phi\otimes1)\rho_n$. For an arbitrary $u:K\to L$, write $A(u)=Rf_*u\otimes1$ and $B(u)=Rf_*(u\otimes1)$. Step 1 gives $B(u)\pi_K=\pi_L A(u)$. Composing with $\rho_L$ on the left and $\rho_K$ on the right gives $\rho_L B(u)=A(u)\rho_K$, since $\rho_L\pi_L=1$ and $\pi_K\rho_K=1$. This proves naturality of the specified inverse wherever it is defined.

proof.text: For the square in the statement, the compatible four coefficient identifications make the induced square of small ringed pro-etale topoi commute. The ambient exchange definition specifies its pullback comparison $\theta:Lf'^*Lg^*\simeq Lg'^*Lf^*$ and declares $\operatorname{Ex}$ to be its mate. The projection arrows in the statement are adjuncts of the counit tensored with identity, using the canonical pullback-tensor comparison. Thus these are precisely the exchange and projection arrows occurring in the general ringed-topos tensor-coherence theorem, with $E=K$ and the same $Q$; none is replaced by an arbitrary isomorphism.

Apply the ringed-topos tensor-coherence theorem to those four topoi and their specified commutation. Its first composite is $\operatorname{Ex}_{K\otimes Lf^*Q}\circ Lg^*(\pi_{f,K,Q})$ and its second is $\pi_{f',Lg'^*K,Lg^*Q}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_K\otimes1)\circ t_g$, exactly the two routes displayed here. Its target identifications are the canonical tensor comparison for $Lg'^*$ and the same $\theta$ on $Q$, as fixed in step 3. Explicitly, the map from the first target to the second is $Rf'_*(1_{Lg'^*K}\otimes\theta_Q^{-1})\circ Rf'_*(t_{g',K,Lf^*Q})$: first apply the pullback-tensor comparison for $g'$, then replace $Lg'^*Lf^*Q$ by $Lf'^*Lg^*Q$ using $\theta_Q^{-1}$. The theorem says that composing the first route with this map gives the second route. This use requires no properness, constructibility, completeness, or invertibility of exchange or projection maps.
